copy.en:
What everyday products are colloids?

Anong mga pang-araw-araw na produkto ang mga colloid?

Ang shampoo, lotion, dishwashing liquid, butter, mayonnaise, hair gel, toothpaste, at ketchup ay mga colloid na ginagamit natin sa pang-araw-araw na gawain tulad ng pagligo at pagluluto.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga adlaw-adlaw nga produkto ang mga colloid?

Ang shampoo, lotion, dishwashing liquid, butter, mayonnaise, hair gel, toothpaste, ug ketchup mga colloid nga atong gigamit sa adlaw-adlaw nga buluhaton sama sa pagkaligo ug pagluto.

Unsang selula sa mata ang makakita og kolor?

Can a girl be color blind if only her father is color blind?

No, a girl needs two affected X chromosomes to be color blind, so she must inherit one from each parent.

Puwede bang maging color blind ang isang babae kung ang tatay lang niya ang color blind?

Hindi, kailangan ng babae ng dalawang apektadong X chromosome para maging color blind, kaya dapat mana siya ng isa sa bawat magulang.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang color blind ang usa ka babaye kung ang iyang amahan lang ang color blind?

Dili, kinahanglan sa babaye og duha ka apektadong X chromosome aron mahimong color blind, busa kinahanglan makapanunod siya og usa sa matag ginikanan.

How do scientists write the equation for burning methane?

Paano isinusulat ng mga scientist ang equation para sa pagsunog ng methane?

Isinusulat nila ang methane plus oxygen ay nagiging carbon dioxide plus water, pagkatapos binabalanse ito sa CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsulat sa mga scientist ang equation para sa pagsunog sa methane?

copy.en: Households commonly generate food and kitchen wastes, papers, plastic bottles, metals and cans, boxes and cartons, glass bottles, cellophane and plastics, and yard or garden wastes.
copy.tl: Ang mga tahanan ay karaniwang gumagawa ng mga basura mula sa pagkain at kusina, papel, plastik na bote, metal at lata, kahon at karton, bote ng salamin, cellophane at plastik, at mga basura sa bakuran o hardin.
copy.bis: Ang mga panimalay kasagarang maggama ug mga basura sa pagkaon ug kusina, papel, plastik nga botelya, metal ug lata, kahon ug karton, botelya nga bildo, cellophane ug plastik, ug mga basura sa nataran o tanaman.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ethyl alcohol, acetone, gasoline, naphthalene, and acetic acid are common organic compounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about common organic compounds and their uses (fuel, cleaners, antiseptics). G7-F-9 requires identifying advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation. The card contains no heat-transfer content and does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ethyl alcohol, acetone, gasoline, naphthalene, and acetic acid are common organic compounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: G7-F-10 requires explaining conduction and convection of heat energy using the particle model. The card discusses organic compounds and their uses, with no mention of heat transfer or particle behavior, so it is unrelated.

copy.en: Ethyl alcohol, acetone, gasoline, naphthalene, and acetic acid are common organic compounds that people use as fuel, cleaners, and antiseptics.
copy.tl: Ang ethyl alcohol, acetone, gasoline, naphthalene, at acetic acid ay mga karaniwang organic compound na ginagamit bilang panggatong, panlinis, at antiseptiko.
copy.bis: Ang ethyl alcohol, acetone, gasoline, naphthalene, ug acetic acid kay kasagarang organic compound nga gigamit isip sugnod, panglimpyo, ug antiseptiko.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most plants have three common parts: roots, stems, and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes common plant parts, not the life cycle stages of animals, and does not use a flow chart. It provides no instructional support for comparing animal life cycles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most plants have three common parts: roots, stems, and leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plant anatomy, not about comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from seed to maturity. It does not address any life-cycle stages.

copy.en: Most plants have three common parts: roots, stems, and leaves, even when these parts look very different from one plant to another.
copy.tl: Karamihan ng mga halaman ay may tatlong karaniwang bahagi: ugat, tangkay, at dahon, kahit na magkakaiba ang itsura ng mga ito sa bawat halaman.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa mga tanom adunay tulo ka kasagarang parte: gamot, stems, ug dahon, bisan pa nga lahi-lahi ang ilang hitsura sa matag tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Communicating results means sharing what you learned from your experiment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the science process skill of communicating results. It contains no information about changes of state, particle arrangement, or energy changes, which are the focus of G7-M-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Communicating results means sharing what you learned from your experiment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sharing experimental findings, not about the role of heat energy in changes of state. It does not support G6-M-2 in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: communicating results
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that a scientist shares findings with other scientists (communicating results). It contains no information about earthquakes, their magnitude, or how earthquake effects on communities depend on magnitude. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: Communicating results means sharing what you learned from your experiment with others, like telling your classmates why you were late because your car ran out of gas.
copy.tl: Ang pagcommunicate ng results ay nangangahulugang pagbabahagi ng iyong natutunan mula sa experiment sa iba, tulad ng pagsasabi sa iyong mga kaklase kung bakit ka na-late dahil naubusan ng gasolina ang iyong sasakyan.
copy.bis: Ang pag-communicate sa results nagpasabot nga ipaambit ang imong nakat-unan gikan sa experiment ngadto sa uban, sama sa pagsulti sa imong mga klasmeyt kon ngano na-late ka tungod kay nahutdan og gasolina ang imong sakyanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solutions to environmental problems can be shared through letters, songs, poems, posters, or diagrams
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses communicating environmental solutions through various media, which is unrelated to the competency of identifying the role of solute and solvent in a chemical solution. The word 'solutions' is used in a non-scientific sense.

copy.en: Solutions to environmental problems can be shared through letters, songs, poems, posters, or diagrams so others can learn and help.
copy.tl: Ang mga solusyon sa problema sa kapaligiran ay maaaring ibahagi sa pamamagitan ng mga liham, kanta, tula, poster, o diagram para matuto at makatulong ang iba.
copy.bis: Ang mga solusyon sa problema sa kinaiyahan mahimong ipaambit pinaagi sa mga sulat, kanta, balak, poster, o diagram aron ang uban makakat-on ug makatabang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Communication skills
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses communication skills for group problem-solving about environmental issues. It has no content about plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) or the transport system, so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Communication skills
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about communication skills, not about observing outer parts of plants or their roles in water and nutrient uptake. It is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: Communication skills, like clearly sharing findings and listening to others, are needed when a group works together to solve environmental issues.
copy.tl: Ang communication skills, tulad ng malinaw na pagbabahagi ng mga natuklasan at pakikinig sa iba, ay kailangan kapag ang grupo ay nagtutulungan para lutasin ang mga isyu sa kapaligiran.
copy.bis: Ang communication skills, sama sa tin-aw nga pagpaambit sa mga nakaplagan ug pagpaminaw sa uban, gikinahanglan kung ang grupo magtinabangay aron sulbaron ang mga isyu sa kinaiyahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind farms can bring benefits like electricity and jobs to a community, but they can also affect local biodiversity, which means the plants and animals living nearby.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses community benefits and biodiversity impacts of wind farms. It contains no information about balanced or unbalanced forces, everyday force situations, or any physics content required by G7-F-2.

copy.en: Wind farms can bring benefits like electricity and jobs to a community, but they can also affect local biodiversity, which means the plants and animals living nearby.
copy.tl: Ang wind farm ay maaaring magdulot ng benepisyo tulad ng kuryente at trabaho sa komunidad, ngunit maaari rin itong makaapekto sa lokal na biodiversity, ibig sabihin ang mga halaman at hayop na nakatira malapit dito.
copy.bis: Ang wind farm makahatag og benepisyo sama sa kuryente ug trabaho sa komunidad, apan makaapekto usab kini sa lokal nga biodiversity, nagpasabot sa mga tanom ug mananap nga nagpuyo duol niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires creating a scale drawing of Earth's interior layers (crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, inner core). The card discusses participating in community cleanup and maintaining peace and order in an evacuation center after a volcanic eruption. There is no connection to Earth's interior structure or scale drawing.

copy.en: After a volcanic eruption, participate in community efforts such as cleaning and maintaining peace and order within the evacuation center.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos ng pagsabog ng bulkan, makilahok sa mga gawain ng komunidad tulad ng paglilinis at pagpapanatili ng kaayusan sa evacuation center.
copy.bis: Human sa pag-ulbo sa bulkan, pag-apil sa mga kalihokan sa komunidad sama sa paglimpyo ug pagmentinar sa kahapsay sa evacuation center.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Community gardens add green spaces to cities and can improve air quality by adding plants that help clean the air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses community gardens and air quality improvement by plants. It contains no example of kinetic energy transforming to potential energy or vice versa, which is the sole subject of G8-F-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Community gardens add green spaces to cities and can improve air quality by adding plants that help clean the air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe kinetic energy as movement or potential energy as stored by position. It is about environmental benefits of gardens, unrelated to the energy concepts in G8-F-4.

copy.en: Community gardens add green spaces to cities and can improve air quality by adding plants that help clean the air.
copy.tl: Ang mga community garden ay nagdadagdag ng luntiang lugar sa siyudad at nakakatulong sa pagpapaganda ng hangin dahil ang mga halaman ay tumutulong maglinis nito.
copy.bis: Ang mga community garden nagdugang og lunhaw nga lugar sa siyudad ug makatabang sa pagpauswag sa hangin kay ang mga tanom makatabang sa paglimpyo sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A community includes all populations of different species living and interacting in an area
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an ecological community, which is unrelated to plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or events. The assigned competency is about Earth and space science (plate tectonics), while the card content is biology/ecology.

copy.en: A community includes all populations of different species living and interacting in an area, like carabaos, grasses, and insects in one field.
copy.tl: Ang community ay binubuo ng lahat ng population ng iba't ibang species na nakatira at nakikipag-ugnayan sa isang lugar, tulad ng mga kalabaw, damo, at insekto sa isang bukid.
copy.bis: Ang community naglakip sa tanang population sa lain-laing species nga nagpuyo ug nag-interact sa usa ka lugar, sama sa mga kabaw, sagbot, ug mga insekto sa usa ka uma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A community's earthquake risk grows when it has old buildings, a dense population, and sits close to an active fault trace.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses earthquake risk factors (building age, population density, proximity to fault). It does not describe changes in material properties due to temperature, such as burning wood or coal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A community's earthquake risk grows when it has old buildings, a dense population, and sits close to an active fault trace.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about earthquake risk, not about chemical change, bond formation, or bond breaking. No chemistry content is present.

copy.en: A community's earthquake risk grows when it has old buildings, a dense population, and sits close to an active fault trace.
copy.tl: Mas tumataas ang earthquake risk ng isang komunidad kapag marami itong lumang gusali, siksikan ang mga tao, at malapit ito sa active fault trace.
copy.bis: Mosaka ang earthquake risk sa usa ka komunidad kon daghan kini og daan nga mga bilding, dasok ang mga tawo, ug duol kini sa active fault trace.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Comparative anatomy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines comparative anatomy and states it provides evidence for evolution. This is a biology/evolution topic and has no instructional support for observing or describing celestial objects in the sky (Sun, Moon, planets, stars).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Comparative anatomy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about comparative anatomy and evolution, not about the Sun's composition, size, or radiated energy. It does not support the G4-E-7 competency in any way.

copy.en: Comparative anatomy is the study of similarities and differences in the body structures of different organisms, and it provides evidence for evolution.
copy.tl: Ang comparative anatomy ay ang pag-aaral ng pagkakatulad at pagkakaiba ng mga bahagi ng katawan ng iba't ibang organismo, at nagbibigay ito ng ebidensya para sa ebolusyon.
copy.bis: Ang comparative anatomy kay ang pagtuon sa pagkapareho ug kalainan sa mga parte sa lawas sa lain-laing mga organismo, ug naghatag kini ug ebidensya alang sa ebolusyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Comparative morphology looks at the similarities and differences in the body structures of organisms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to identify and describe examples of innovative devices that can be used to transform heat energy into electrical energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about comparative morphology (biology), not about innovative devices transforming heat energy into electrical energy. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Comparative morphology looks at the similarities and differences in the body structures of organisms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses body structure comparisons, not sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy. Unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Comparative anatomy is the study of body structures in different animals, and it helps scientists find clues about how species are related.
copy.tl: Ang comparative anatomy ay ang pag-aaral ng mga bahagi ng katawan ng iba't ibang hayop, at nakakatulong ito sa mga scientist na malaman kung paano magkakaugnay ang mga species.
copy.bis: Ang comparative anatomy mao ang pagtuon sa mga parte sa lawas sa lain-laing mga mananap, ug kini makatabang sa mga scientist nga mahibalo kung giunsa pagka-ugnay ang mga species.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If two communities both have 50 individuals and 5 species, can one be more diverse?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw diagrams of and assemble series and parallel circuits, showing switch, battery, loads/resistors, ammeter, and voltmeter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses community diversity, evenness, and dominance in an ecological context. G9-F-8 requires drawing and assembling series and parallel circuits with specific components. There is no electrical circuit content, so the tag is unrelated.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If two communities both have 50 individuals and 5 species, can one be more diverse?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about comparing species diversity and evenness, not about assembling or drawing a simple circuit. G5-F-8 explicitly requires a simple circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer, which is absent. The tag is unrelated.

copy.en:
If two communities both have 50 individuals and 5 species, can one be more diverse?

Yes! Community A with 10 individuals per species has greater evenness, while Community B with 20, 10, 10, 6, and 4 individuals has greater variation in dominance.
copy.tl:
Kung ang dalawang komunidad ay parehong may 50 indibidwal at 5 species, maaari bang mas diverse ang isa?

Oo! Ang Community A na may 10 indibidwal bawat species ay may mas mataas na evenness, habang ang Community B na may 20, 10, 10, 6, at 4 na indibidwal ay may mas malaking variation sa dominance.
copy.bis:
Kon ang duha ka komunidad pareho nga adunay 50 ka indibidwal ug 5 ka species, mahimo bang mas diverse ang usa?

Oo! Ang Community A nga adunay 10 ka indibidwal matag species adunay mas taas nga evenness, samtang ang Community B nga adunay 20, 10, 10, 6, ug 4 ka indibidwal adunay mas dako nga variation sa dominance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Compare their lengths by measuring from tip to base along the longest part.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to measure and compare leaf lengths, which is unrelated to identifying advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation (heat transfer).

copy.en:
How can I find the shortest and longest leaves?

Compare their lengths by measuring from tip to base along the longest part.
copy.tl:
Paano ko malalaman kung alin ang pinakamaikli at pinakamahabang dahon?

Ikumpara mo ang haba ng mga ito sa pamamagitan ng pagsukat mula dulo hanggang base sa pinakamahabang bahagi.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nako pagkahibalo kung asa ang pinakamubo ug pinakataas nga dahon?

Itandi ang ilang gitas-on pinaagi sa pagsukod sugod sa tumoy paingon sa punoan sa pinakataas nga parte.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Measure them with a ruler!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches comparing leaf sizes by measuring length and width with a ruler. G5-F-7 requires investigating static electricity using materials like combs, rods, and balloons. There is no connection to static electricity, forces, or electricity; the content is unrelated.

copy.en:
If two leaves look almost the same size, how can you tell which is longer or wider?

Measure them with a ruler! Comparing their measured length and width in a table shows the real difference.
copy.tl:
Kung halos magkapareho ang laki ng dalawang dahon, paano mo malalaman kung alin ang mas mahaba o mas malapad?

Sukatin mo sila gamit ang ruler! Ang paghahambing ng kanilang nasukat na haba at lapad sa isang table ay nagpapakita ng totoong pagkakaiba.
copy.bis:
Kung halos managsama ang gidak-on sa duha ka dahon, giunsa nimo pagkahibalo kung hain ang mas taas o mas lapad?

Sukda sila gamit ang ruler! Ang pagtandi sa ilang nasukod nga gitas-on ug gilapdon sa usa ka table nagpakita sa tinuod nga kalainan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Organizing data into a table
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses organizing data into tables for comparison and pattern analysis. It contains no information about volcanoes, their formation, or volcanic activity, which is the subject of G6-E-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Organizing data into a table
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about data organization and comparison, not about describing types of volcanoes according to activity, eruption type, or crustal location. It does not support G8-E-3 in any way.

copy.en: Organizing data into a table allows you to compare items, analyze results, and spot patterns to make conclusions.
copy.tl: Ang pag-aayos ng datos sa isang table ay nagbibigay-daan sa iyo upang maihambing ang mga bagay, masuri ang mga resulta, at makita ang mga pattern para makagawa ng konklusyon.
copy.bis: Ang pag-organisar sa datos sa usa ka table nagtugot kanimo sa pagtandi sa mga butang, pag-analisar sa mga resulta, ug pagtan-aw sa mga pattern aron makahimo og konklusyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Male and female reproductive systems can be compared by their primary organs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the comparison of male and female reproductive systems, a biology topic. G9-F-11 is about comparing wavelengths and frequencies of electromagnetic waves, which is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: Male and female reproductive systems can be compared by their primary organs, which make sex cells, their secondary organs, and their accessory organs that support reproduction.
copy.tl: Ang male at female reproductive systems ay maaaring paghambingin sa pamamagitan ng primary organs na gumagawa ng sex cells, secondary organs, at accessory organs na tumutulong sa reproduction.
copy.bis: Ang male ug female reproductive systems mahimong itandi pinaagi sa primary organs nga mohimo ug sex cells, secondary organs, ug accessory organs nga motabang sa reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Which sports drink has more electrolytes: 75% in 500 mL, or 400 mL solvent in 500 mL solution?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about comparing solute amounts and percentage concentration in solutions. It does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space, nor does it support that competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Which sports drink has more electrolytes: 75% in 500 mL, or 400 mL solvent in 500 mL solution?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card has no connection to gravity or non-contact forces. It is entirely about solution concentration and solute/solvent quantities.

copy.en:
Which sports drink has more electrolytes: 75% in 500 mL, or 400 mL solvent in 500 mL solution?

The first has 375 mL of solute, while the second has only 100 mL, so the 75% drink has more!
copy.tl:
Aling sports drink ang may mas maraming electrolytes: 75% sa 500 mL, o 400 mL solvent sa 500 mL solution?

Ang una ay may 375 mL na solute, habang ang pangalawa ay may 100 mL lamang, kaya ang 75% na inumin ay may mas marami!
copy.bis:
Hain nga sports drink ang adunay mas daghan nga electrolytes: 75% sa 500 mL, o 400 mL solvent sa 500 mL solution?

Ang una adunay 375 mL nga solute, samtang ang ikaduha adunay 100 mL lamang, busa ang 75% nga ilimnon adunay mas daghan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A measurement is just comparing an object to a standard.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the concept of measurement as comparison to a standard. It contains no information about weather characteristics (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover) and does not support identifying any weather descriptors. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en:
Why do we need a standard when measuring?

A measurement is just comparing an object to a standard. Without a standard, everyone would get a different answer for the same thing!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan natin ng standard kapag sumusukat?

Ang pagsukat ay paghahambing lamang ng isang bagay sa isang standard. Kapag walang standard, iba-iba ang makukuhang sagot ng bawat isa sa iisang bagay!
copy.bis:
Ngano kinahanglan man nato ug standard kon magsukod?

Ang pagsukod mao ra ang pagtandi sa usa ka butang ngadto sa usa ka standard. Kon walay standard, lain-lain ang makuha nga tubag sa matag usa sa usa ra ka butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Competition is the striving or vying between organisms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines biological competition among organisms for survival needs. G4-F-7 requires guided investigations into the properties of magnets and their effects on other magnets and materials. The card has no connection to magnets, forces, or any physics content.

copy.en: Competition is the striving or vying between organisms for the things needed for survival, like food, water, sunlight, and space.
copy.tl: Ang competition ay ang pag-aagawan o paglalaban ng mga organismo para sa mga bagay na kailangan upang mabuhay, tulad ng pagkain, tubig, sikat ng araw, at espasyo.
copy.bis: Ang competition mao ang pag-ilogay o paglalis sa mga organismo para sa mga butang nga gikinahanglan aron mabuhi, sama sa pagkaon, tubig, kahayag sa adlaw, ug espasyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: For electrons to flow continuously, there must be a complete circuit with no gaps, so a break anywhere stops the current everywhere.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Circuit continuity is electricity, not plant reproduction.

copy.en: For electrons to flow continuously, there must be a complete circuit with no gaps, so a break anywhere stops the current everywhere.
copy.tl: Para tuloy-tuloy ang daloy ng mga electron, kailangan kumpleto ang circuit na walang puwang, kaya kapag may naputol kahit saan, hihinto ang current sa lahat ng bahagi.
copy.bis: Aron padayon ang pag-agos sa mga electron, kinahanglan kompleto ang circuit nga walay puwang, busa kung adunay maputol bisan asa, mohunong ang current sa tanang parte.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many flowers are complete because they have both male parts, the stamens, and female parts, the pistil, in the same bloom.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes flower anatomy (presence of stamens and pistil), which is unrelated to predicting genotype/phenotype ratios in dominant/recessive crosses. It does not support the genetics competency.

copy.en: Many flowers are complete because they have both male parts, the stamens, and female parts, the pistil, in the same bloom.
copy.tl: Maraming bulaklak ay kumpleto dahil mayroon silang parehong male parts, ang stamens, at female parts, ang pistil, sa iisang pamumulaklak.
copy.bis: Daghang bulaklak ang kompleto tungod kay aduna silay parehong male parts, ang stamens, ug female parts, ang pistil, sa usa ra ka pagpamulak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why are parallel circuits more complicated to design than series circuits?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the design complexity of parallel versus series electrical circuits. G9-M-11 is about investigating properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances (melting point, hardness, conductivity). The card has no connection to chemical bonding or substance properties; it is a physics/electrical topic, so the tag is wrong.

copy.en:
Why are parallel circuits more complicated to design than series circuits?

They need more wires and careful planning because each branch must be connected separately to the source.

Sa conclusion, isulti kung ang imong hypothesis gisuportahan sa data. Gamita ang mga numero gikan sa imong resulta isip ebidensya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A conclusion must answer the original aim or problem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains what a scientific conclusion should do (answer the aim using data). It has no content about changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or diagrams/flowcharts of state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A conclusion must answer the original aim or problem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about writing a conclusion in a scientific investigation, not about how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). No relevant instructional support.

copy.en:
What should a conclusion always do?

A conclusion must answer the original aim or problem, using the data you collected to say whether your idea was right or wrong!
copy.tl:
Ano ang dapat laging gawin ng isang conclusion?

Dapat sagutin ng conclusion ang orihinal na aim o problem, gamit ang datos na iyong nakalap para sabihin kung tama o mali ang iyong ideya!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kinahanglan kanunay nga buhaton sa usa ka conclusion?

Kinahanglan tubagon sa conclusion ang orihinal nga aim o problem, gamit ang datos nga imong nakolekta aron isulti kung husto ba o sayop ang imong ideya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A compound microscope has a condenser
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes microscope parts (condenser, illuminator), not simple machines or their advantages/limitations. No support for G6-F-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A compound microscope has a condenser
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about microscope components, not examples and uses of simple machines. Unrelated to G6-F-1.

copy.en: A compound microscope has a condenser to focus light and an illuminator to shine light through the specimen, but a simple microscope uses only natural light.
copy.tl: Ang compound microscope ay may condenser para ituon ang liwanag at illuminator para magpasikat ng liwanag sa specimen, pero ang simple microscope ay gumagamit lamang ng natural na liwanag.
copy.bis: Ang compound microscope adunay condenser aron ipunting ang kahayag ug illuminator aron modan-ag sa specimen, apan ang simple microscope naggamit lamang ug natural nga kahayag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To test a hypothesis, you design and conduct an experiment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes designing and conducting an experiment to test a hypothesis, which is a general scientific process skill. It does not address examining a local weather chart, interpreting local weather, or describing/practicing safety precautions for poor or extreme weather conditions, which are the specific actions of G4-E-6.

copy.en: To test a hypothesis, you design and conduct an experiment — a scientific procedure to test an idea and make a discovery.
copy.tl: Para masubok ang hypothesis, nagdidisenyo at nagsasagawa ka ng experiment — isang siyentipikong pamamaraan para subukin ang isang ideya at gumawa ng pagtuklas.
copy.bis: Aron masulayan ang hypothesis, magdisenyo ug magpahigayon ka og experiment — usa ka siyentipikong pamaagi sa pagsulay sa usa ka ideya ug paghimo og diskobre.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charging by conduction is carried out by bringing two objects into direct contact
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrostatic charging by conduction, a physics topic. G10-L-3 concerns natural selection as the mechanism of evolutionary change, which is unrelated to the card's content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Charging by conduction is carried out by bringing two objects into direct contact
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses conduction charging, not evolution concepts such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation. No instructional support for G10-L-4.

copy.en: Charging by conduction is carried out by bringing two objects into direct contact with each other, not just close together.
copy.tl: Ang charging by conduction ay isinasagawa sa pamamagitan ng direktang pagdikit ng dalawang bagay sa isa't isa, hindi lamang paglapit sa kanila.
copy.bis: Ang charging by conduction gihimo pinaagi sa direktang paghikap sa duha ka butang sa usag usa, dili lamang pagpaduol kanila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conduction is the transfer of heat or electricity from one object to another
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines conduction (transfer of heat or electricity), which is a physics concept. G8-M-3 requires differentiating subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) by symbol, mass, charge, and location. The card provides no information about subatomic particles or atomic structure, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en: Conduction is the transfer of heat or electricity from one object to another, or from one molecule to another.
copy.tl: Ang conduction ay ang paglipat ng init o kuryente mula sa isang bagay patungo sa iba, o mula sa isang molecule patungo sa iba.
copy.bis: Ang conduction mao ang pagbalhin sa kainit o kuryente tali sa usa ka butang ngadto sa lain, o tali sa usa ka molecule ngadto sa lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Good heat conductors are usually solid, hard, ductile, malleable, and have compact molecules packed closely together.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes physical properties of heat conductors, which is a physics/materials topic. G6-E-5 requires interpreting PHIVOLCS volcano alert levels and safety actions before, during, and after a volcanic eruption. There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: Good heat conductors are usually solid, hard, ductile, malleable, and have compact molecules packed closely together.
copy.tl: Ang mahuhusay na heat conductors ay kadalasang solid, matigas, ductile, malleable, at may mga compact molecule na magkakadikit.
copy.bis: Ang maayo nga heat conductors kasagarang solid, gahi, ductile, malleable, ug adunay mga compact molecule nga nagkaduol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Living and non-living things are interconnected, meaning they affect and need each other in the environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Living/non-living interconnection is unrelated to the circulatory system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they affect and need each other in the environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Ecosystem interconnection is not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems.

copy.en: Living and non-living things are interconnected, meaning they affect and need each other in the environment.
copy.tl: Ang mga may buhay at walang buhay ay magkaugnay, ibig sabihin nakakaapekto at nangangailangan sila sa isa't isa sa kapaligiran.
copy.bis: Ang mga may kinabuhi ug walay kinabuhi magkaugnay, nagpasabot nga makaapekto ug nagkinahanglan sila sa usag usa sa kalikopan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The peripheral nervous system connects the central nervous system to the organs and limbs.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the peripheral nervous system, which is unrelated to expressing quantitatively the amount of solute in a given volume of solvent (concentration).

copy.en: The peripheral nervous system connects the central nervous system to the organs and limbs.
copy.tl: Ang peripheral nervous system ay nag-uugnay sa central nervous system sa mga organ at limbs.
copy.bis: Ang peripheral nervous system nagkonekta sa central nervous system ngadto sa mga organ ug limbs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: total mechanical energy is conserved
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about conservation of mechanical energy in an isolated system, which is a physics topic. G6-M-4 requires describing everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions). There is no overlap in content.

copy.en: In an isolated system with only conservative forces, total mechanical energy is conserved, meaning it remains constant over time.
copy.tl: Sa isang isolated system na may conservative forces lamang, ang total mechanical energy ay conserved, ibig sabihin nananatili itong pareho sa paglipas ng panahon.
copy.bis: Sa usa ka isolated system nga adunay conservative forces lamang, ang total mechanical energy gi-conserve, nagpasabot nga kini nagpabilin nga pareho sa paglabay sa panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The number of valence electrons before and after covalent bonding stays the same
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses conservation of valence electrons in covalent bonding, a chemistry topic. G6-E-9 is about ancient cultures using constellations for direction and seasons, which is unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: The number of valence electrons before and after covalent bonding stays the same, following the Law of Conservation of Matter.
copy.tl: Ang bilang ng valence electrons bago at pagkatapos ng covalent bonding ay nananatiling pareho, alinsunod sa Law of Conservation of Matter.
copy.bis: Ang gidaghanon sa valence electrons sa wala pa ug pagkahuman sa covalent bonding nagpabilin nga pareho, subay sa Law of Conservation of Matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The force vector on a projectile remains constant throughout flight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the force vector on a projectile (physics), not about observing or describing animal outer body parts or their roles in movement and feeding. No instructional support for G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The force vector on a projectile remains constant throughout flight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about projectile motion and gravity, not about classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram. No instructional support for G4-L-3.

copy.en: The force vector on a projectile remains constant throughout flight: it always points straight down with the same length, because gravity is the only force acting on it.
copy.tl: Ang force vector sa projectile ay nananatiling constant sa buong paglipad: laging nakaturo diretso pababa na may parehong haba, dahil gravity lang ang puwersang kumikilos dito.
copy.bis: Ang force vector sa projectile nagpabilin nga constant sa tibuok paglupad: kanunay nagpunting tul-id paubos nga parehas og gitas-on, tungod kay gravity ra ang puwersa nga naglihok kaniya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The word constellation comes from the Latin word 'con' meaning group and 'stella' meaning stars.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the etymology of the word 'constellation'. It has no connection to biotechnology, fermentation, or traditional biotechnology products (cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The word constellation comes from the Latin word 'con' meaning group and 'stella' meaning stars.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the term biotechnology and provide examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the origin of the term 'constellation' in astronomy, not about biotechnology or its definition/examples. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The word constellation comes from the Latin word 'con' meaning group and 'stella' meaning stars.
copy.tl: Ang salitang constellation ay nagmula sa Latin na 'con' na ibig sabihin ay grupo at 'stella' na ibig sabihin ay mga bituin.
copy.bis: Ang pulong nga constellation naggikan sa Latin nga 'con' nga nagpasabot og grupo ug 'stella' nga nagpasabot og mga bituon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Popular beliefs about zodiac signs and horoscopes do not have a scientific basis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses constellations and astrology, which is unrelated to traditional biotechnology through fermentation (cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco). No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Popular beliefs about zodiac signs and horoscopes do not have a scientific basis, even though constellations themselves are real.
copy.tl: Ang mga popular na paniniwala tungkol sa zodiac signs at horoscope ay walang scientific basis, kahit na totoo naman ang mga constellation mismo.
copy.bis: Ang mga popular nga pagtuo mahitungod sa zodiac signs ug horoscope walay scientific basis, bisan tuod tinuod ang mga constellation mismo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Filipino ancestors observed the stars
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify the products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (e.g. cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ancestral star observation for planting/harvest timing, which is astronomy/constellations. G10-L-7 is about identifying products of traditional biotechnology through fermentation (cheese, soy sauce, vinegar, nata de coco). No connection to fermentation or biotechnology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Filipino ancestors observed the stars
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about constellations used as a guide for decisions, not about unicellular vs multicellular organisms. G7-L-3 requires recognizing single-celled vs multi-celled organisms, which is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Filipino ancestors observed the stars as a guide for making major decisions, such as choosing the right month to plant and harvest.
copy.tl: Pinagmasdan ng mga ninunong Pilipino ang mga bituin bilang gabay sa paggawa ng mahahalagang desisyon, tulad ng pagpili ng tamang buwan para magtanim at mag-ani.
copy.bis: Gibantayan sa mga katigulangang Pilipino ang mga bituon isip giya sa paghimo og dagkong mga desisyon, sama sa pagpili sa saktong bulan aron magtanom ug mag-ani.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Circumpolar constellations like Ursa Major, Cassiopeia, Ursa Minor, and Cygnus can be seen all year round because they circle the North Star.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about astronomy (constellations), not about animals and plants in a habitat. It does not support making a list or table of organisms in a named habitat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Circumpolar constellations like Ursa Major, Cassiopeia, Ursa Minor, and Cygnus can be seen all year round because they circle the North Star.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses constellations, which are non-living celestial objects, and does not address interactions between living things or between living and non-living things bringing good or harm.

copy.en: Circumpolar constellations like Ursa Major, Cassiopeia, Ursa Minor, and Cygnus can be seen all year round because they circle the North Star.
copy.tl: Ang mga circumpolar constellation tulad ng Ursa Major, Cassiopeia, Ursa Minor, at Cygnus ay nakikita sa buong taon dahil umiikot sila sa North Star.
copy.bis: Ang mga circumpolar constellation sama sa Ursa Major, Cassiopeia, Ursa Minor, ug Cygnus makita sa tibuok tuig tungod kay nagtuyok sila libot sa North Star.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To make a line graph
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that momentum depends on the mass and the velocity of a moving object that can be used to predict the impact the object will have if it hits another object
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to construct a line graph, which is a graphing/mathematical skill. The competency G10-F-4 is about momentum depending on mass and velocity to predict impact. There is no instructional support for momentum, mass, velocity, or collisions.

copy.en: To make a line graph, first label the axes, then determine your variables, choose a scale, plot the points, connect them with a line, and add a title.
copy.tl: Para gumawa ng line graph, lagyan muna ng labels ang mga axes, alamin ang variables, pumili ng scale, i-plot ang mga points, pagdugtungin ng line, at lagyan ng title.
copy.bis: Aron maghimo og line graph, butangi una og labels ang mga axes, tinoa ang variables, pagpili og scale, i-plot ang mga points, dugtunga og line, ug butangi og title.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pushing a chair, carrying a bag by its handle, and sliding a box on a table are all examples of contact forces in everyday life.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about contact forces in daily life, which is a physics/force topic. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, and their features. There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: Pushing a chair, carrying a bag by its handle, and sliding a box on a table are all examples of contact forces in everyday life.
copy.tl: Ang pagtulak ng upuan, pagbitbit ng bag sa hawakan nito, at pag-slide ng kahon sa mesa ay mga halimbawa ng contact forces sa pang-araw-araw na buhay.
copy.bis: Ang pagtulod sa lingkuranan, pagdala sa bag pinaagi sa gunitanan, ug pag-slide sa kahon sa lamesa mga pananglitan sa contact forces sa adlaw-adlaw nga kinabuhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Contact forces happen when two objects touch each other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains contact forces (a physics/force concept), while G6-M-6 requires demonstrating mixture separation techniques such as decantation, filtering, and sieving. There is no overlap in content.

copy.en: Contact forces happen when two objects touch each other, like your hand pushing a book across a table.
copy.tl: Ang contact forces ay nangyayari kapag magkadikit ang dalawang bagay, tulad ng kamay mo na nagtutulak ng libro sa mesa.
copy.bis: Ang contact forces mahitabo kung magtandog ang duha ka butang, sama sa imong kamot nga nagtulod sa libro sa lamesa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a public health method that finds and notifies people who may have been exposed to a disease
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes contact tracing, a public health/epidemiology method for disease control. G6-L-8 requires explaining how interactions between living things and between living and non-living things bring good or harm in an ecological context. Contact tracing is unrelated to ecological interactions and does not support this competency.

copy.en:
What is contact tracing?

It's a public health method that finds and notifies people who may have been exposed to a disease, to help stop it from spreading.
copy.tl:
Ano ang contact tracing?

Isa itong pamamaraan ng public health na naghahanap at nagpapaalam sa mga taong maaaring nalantad sa sakit, para matulungang mapigilan ang paglaganap nito.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang contact tracing?

Kini usa ka pamaagi sa public health nga mangita ug mopahibalo sa mga tawo nga posibleng nalantad sa sakit, aron matabangan nga mapugngan ang pagkaylap niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: continental crust
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use the PHIVOLCS FaultFinder or other reliable information source to identify where the nearest fault system is located from their community and assess the risk of earthquakes to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the composition and density of the continental crust. The competency requires using PHIVOLCS FaultFinder or another reliable source to locate the nearest fault system and assess earthquake risk to the local community. The card provides no information about faults, fault systems, PHIVOLCS, risk assessment, or community safety, and is therefore unrelated to the assigned competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Continental crust is the thick part of the Earth's crust
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes continental crust, a geology/earth science topic, and provides no information about using a microscope or identifying cell parts (cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, chloroplasts). The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: The land we live on is part of the continental crust, a thick layer of granite rock that is less dense, so it floats higher on the mantle.
copy.tl: Ang lupang ating tinitirhan ay bahagi ng continental crust, isang makapal na layer ng granite rock na hindi gaanong siksik, kaya mas mataas itong lumulutang sa mantle.
copy.bis: Ang yuta nga atong gipuy-an kabahin sa continental crust, usa ka baga nga layer sa granite rock nga dili kaayo dasok, mao nga mas taas kini nga naglutaw sa mantle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: landforms found on continental crust
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes landforms on continental crust, which is an Earth science topic. G6-M-4 requires describing everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions). There is no connection to mixtures, solutions, or suspensions.

copy.en: Plains, mountain ranges, and plateaus are landforms found on continental crust, which forms the continents and larger landmasses.
copy.tl: Ang mga kapatagan, bulubundukin, at talampas ay mga anyong lupa na matatagpuan sa continental crust, na bumubuo sa mga kontinente at malalaking landmass.
copy.bis: Ang mga kapatagan, kabukiran, ug talampas mao ang mga porma sa yuta nga makita sa continental crust, nga nagporma sa mga kontinente ug dagkong landmass.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The continental drift theory states that Earth's continents were once joined together in a single landmass and have slowly moved apart over millions of years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains continental drift, a geological concept about the movement of continents. G7-L-8 requires using a labelled diagram to describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere. The card provides no biological organization content and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: The continental drift theory states that Earth's continents were once joined together in a single landmass and have slowly moved apart over millions of years.
copy.tl: Sinasabi ng continental drift theory na ang mga kontinente ng Earth ay dating magkakadikit sa isang malaking lupain at dahan-dahang nagkahiwalay sa loob ng milyun-milyong taon.
copy.bis: Ang continental drift theory nag-ingon nga ang mga kontinente sa Earth kaniadto nagkahiusa sa usa ka dako nga yuta ug hinay-hinay nga nagbulag sa minilyon ka mga tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When an oceanic plate subducts beneath a continental plate, the rising magma creates a line of volcanoes on the continent called a volcanic arc.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes continental volcanic arcs formed by subduction, which is an Earth science topic. G7-L-2 requires using a microscope to observe and identify cell parts (cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, chloroplasts). There is no connection to cells, microscopes, or biology.

copy.en: When an oceanic plate subducts beneath a continental plate, the rising magma creates a line of volcanoes on the continent called a volcanic arc.
copy.tl: Kapag ang oceanic plate ay sumusubduct sa ilalim ng continental plate, ang umaakyat na magma ay bumubuo ng hanay ng mga bulkan sa kontinente na tinatawag na volcanic arc.
copy.bis: Kung ang oceanic plate mag-subduct ilawom sa continental plate, ang mosaka nga magma moporma ug laray sa mga bulkan sa kontinente nga gitawag ug volcanic arc.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Contour farming is a sustainable way of farming
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes contour farming, an agricultural soil-conservation practice. It provides no information about comets, meteoroids, asteroids, dwarf planets, or the formation of the Earth and Solar System, so it does not support this competency at all.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Contour farming is a sustainable way of farming
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about contour farming, not the structure of the solar system or celestial objects. It is entirely unrelated to this astronomy competency.

copy.en: Contour farming is a sustainable way of farming where farmers plant crops across or perpendicular to slopes to follow the contours of a field.
copy.tl: Ang contour farming ay isang sustainable na paraan ng pagsasaka kung saan nagtatanim ang mga magsasaka ng mga pananim nang pahalang o patayo sa mga slope upang sundan ang mga contour ng bukid.
copy.bis: Ang contour farming usa ka sustainable nga pamaagi sa pag-uma diin ang mga mag-uuma nagtanom sa mga tanom nga pahigda o patindog sa mga slope aron sundon ang mga contour sa uma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Contour plowing is a farming technique
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a soil conservation farming practice to slow erosion. It has no content about animal reproduction (live birth vs egg-laying), so it does not support G5-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Contour plowing is a farming technique
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about contour plowing and soil erosion, not about comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants. It does not support G5-L-6.

copy.en: Contour plowing is a farming technique where soil is plowed following the shape of the land, which helps slow down soil erosion.
copy.tl: Ang contour plowing ay paraan ng pagsasaka kung saan inaararo ang lupa ayon sa hugis ng lupain, na nakakatulong para mapabagal ang soil erosion.
copy.bis: Ang contour plowing usa ka pamaagi sa pagpanguma diin ang yuta giarado subay sa porma sa yuta, nga makatabang sa pagpahinay sa soil erosion.
